We analyze the CS (J = 2 - 1) line cube from the internal data release obtained by the large-scale program "ALMA CMZ Exploration Survey (ACES)" to investigate the kinematic structure of the innermost ~ 10 pc region of the Galaxy

In this paper, we examine the kinematics of the LV features of G0.02 and related structures from the point of view of galactic dynamics by analyzing the 3D cube of the CS (J = 2 - 1 ) line emission observed with ALMA by ACES.

Because G0.02 is located near the tangential direction of this ellipse, the width of the molecular line increases to several tens km s^{-1} due to shear in orbital velocity.

The cloud is strongly stretched to make a spiral shape and loses its identity within one orbital rotation. Since such a compact cloud can easily be disrupted, it is generally difficult for any molecular cloud to survive disruption in the central 10 pc.

The projected shape in the sky and the global elliptical LVD of G0.02 are generally explained by the eccentric orbit model in the gravitational potential due to an extended mass distribution. However, the O -type LV feature is better reproduced by the expanding-ring model, and the high-velocity LV wing is explained by the SN-induced local expansion model. So, we cannot rule out these models at this time.

Because G0.02 is located near the tangential direction of this ellipse, the width of the molecular line increases to several tens km s^{-1} due to shear in orbital velocity. G+0.02-0.02+100 is thus a kinematic tracer of the inner potential, a rare case of a dense gas following an eccentric orbit in the nuclear gravitational field.

all_quotes.quote: it is generally difficult for any molecular cloud to survive disruption in the central 10 pc. Therefore, it is more natural to consider that G0.02 is a part of the rotating disc as an arm or a wave

The cloud is strongly stretched to make a spiral shape and loses its identity within one orbital rotation. Since such a compact cloud can easily be disrupted, it is generally difficult for any molecular cloud to survive disruption in the central 10 pc. Therefore, it is more natural to consider that G0.02 is a part of the rotating disc as an arm or a wave orbiting around the potential of the central bulge.

So, we restricted our analysis to the CS (J = 2 - 1 ) line that covers -220 \le v_LSR \le 220 km s^{-1} .
